title: In a market sizing case, state a rough guess first, build the estimate in steps and cross-check it
description: The first question to ask in a market sizing case, how to structure it, and the trap to avoid.
hook: Market sizing questions can turn up on their own or in the middle of a bigger case. Here is the approach that works for both.
body:
The first question to ask

Units or value? Which geography? Any limiting factor?

How to build your structure

  1. Say a rough guess first (your hypothesis)
  2. Choose top-down (from buyers) or bottom-up (from sellers)
  3. Split into segments where it matters
  4. Use round numbers and say you are rounding
  5. Sanity-check the answer from another direction

The trap most people fall into

No answer hypothesis; no cross-check.

An example

Here is the routine in action for "How big is the UK market for dog grooming?" Clarify: value, per year, UK only. Hypothesis: probably a few hundred million pounds. Approach: dogs in the UK, times the share professionally groomed, times visits a year, times price. Round: 12 million dogs, 30% groomed, 4 visits, £40 a visit gives about £575 million. Sanity check: around £50 per dog per year sounds plausible.

How it sounds in an interview

Before I size it, my rough guess is a few hundred million pounds. I'll build it from the number of dogs and check it against what an owner spends in a year.
